Key To Terms Used

SEGMENTATION Splitting an image into regions, for example separating cheek, forehead, and background.

LANDMARK Reference points on a face, used to align images so that they can be compared.

BASELINE The simple method a new method has to beat before it is worth anything.

FAILURE MODE The specific condition under which a method stops working, such as poor lighting.

PREPROCESSING Cleaning and standardizing images before any analysis runs.

REPRODUCIBLE A pipeline another engineer can rerun from the repository and get the same result.

Intended Role

The initiative asks whether standardized facial images can be turned into structured, useful skin insights. Nobody has decided that it works. This role runs the experiments that answer it. You will build preprocessing pipelines, test detection and segmentation approaches, and report honestly on where they break. The emphasis is on rigorous, reproducible feasibility testing, not on shipping a finished model.

Principal Duties

– Build reproducible preprocessing pipelines covering normalization, alignment, lighting correction, and quality gating.

– Test and compare open-source face detection, landmark, and region segmentation methods on sample images.

– Implement and evaluate candidate visual feature measures for skin characteristics such as texture, tone, and evenness of appearance.

– Design controlled experiments that isolate one variable at a time, and record settings so results can be reproduced.

– Quantify failure modes, including lighting, camera, angle, and skin tone effects, and report them without softening.

– Document every pipeline and experiment so another engineer can rerun it from the repository alone.

– Use approved AI coding tools to accelerate implementation, then verify behavior with unit tests and by inspecting outputs by hand.

Example Assignments

Assignments depend on active studies, authorized data access, and the internship timeline. Examples may include: – A preprocessing and quality-gate pipeline that standardizes incoming facial images

– A benchmark comparing detection and segmentation methods on accuracy, speed, and failure modes

– A feasibility report on whether a proposed visual feature can be measured reliably enough to be useful

Your First Two Weeks

– Set up the environment and reproduce one published baseline on sample images.

– Build the preprocessing pipeline and run it over the first batch end to end.

– Benchmark two detection methods and record accuracy, speed, and where each fails.

– Write the experiment log format for the rest of the placement.

Data Science Intern, Dataset Curation & Model Evaluation

Educational partner referral. Candidates apply through their education partner with a CV and short note, followed by a conversation with the project lead.

Work arrangement: Remote / Onsite.

Key To Terms Used

ANNOTATION Human-assigned labels on data. The definition matters more than the tool.

AGREEMENT How often two independent annotators give the same label to the same item.

SPLIT Keeping training and test data separate so that results are not self-congratulatory.

SUBGROUP Performance reported per group, rather than one average that hides a failure.

LICENSE The terms under which a dataset may legally be used, including for commercial work.

THRESHOLD The success bar set before results exist, and not moved afterwards.

Intended Role

Before a health AI model can be trusted, someone has to define what the data means and what counts as good enough. This role does that upstream work. You will survey available datasets and their licenses, design annotation schemas, and build the evaluation framework the project will be judged against. The emphasis is on defining measurement honestly before results exist, not on chasing a headline accuracy number.

Principal Duties

– Survey publicly available image and health datasets, documenting content, licensing terms, and stated limitations.

– Assess dataset representativeness across demographics, capture conditions, and label quality, and state gaps plainly.

– Design annotation schemas and written labeling guidelines that two independent annotators could apply consistently.

– Measure annotation agreement, and revise guidelines where disagreement shows the definition is ambiguous.

– Define the evaluation framework, including metrics, splits, baselines, and success thresholds, before any comparison.

– Run subgroup and bias analyses so that reported performance is not an average hiding an unacceptable failure.

– Use approved AI tools for exploration and drafting, then verify all dataset claims against the original documentation.

Example Assignments

Assignments depend on active studies, authorized data access, and the internship timeline. Examples may include: – A dataset landscape review with licensing, representativeness, and suitability recommendations

– An annotation schema and labeling guideline with an inter- annotator agreement study

– An evaluation framework defining metrics, baselines, splits, and subgroup reporting requirements

Your First Two Weeks

– Survey candidate datasets and record content, license terms, and stated limitations.

– Draft the first annotation guideline and label a pilot set yourself.

– Run a two-annotator pilot and measure how often the labels agree.

– Propose the metrics, splits, and success thresholds before any model is compared.

Start with your education partner. The referral process uses a CV and a short note, followed by a conversation with the project lead. Confirm current availability and placement arrangements through that process.

Interns who complete the program receive a certificate of completion on company letterhead. A letter of recommendation is available on completion.
